questions.question: An if-statement in Python is used to execute code only when a condition is True.
In Python, an if-statement must always include an else clause.
An if-statement in Python can test for equality using the '==' operator.
The 'elif' keyword in Python is a shorthand for 'else if' and is used to test additional conditions sequentially.
In nested if-statements, the inner if condition is evaluated even if the outer if condition is False.
Python allows chaining of comparison operators (e.g., 0 < x < 5) in an if-statement without the need for logical operators.
In Python, the condition of an if-statement must be enclosed within parentheses.
An if-elif-else chain in Python can have multiple elif clauses but only one else clause at the end.
Using multiple separate if-statements to test mutually exclusive conditions is generally more efficient than an if-elif chain in Python.
When an if-statement condition in Python involves multiple logical operators, the expressions are evaluated using short-circuit logic.
